---
title: "Panels and cards"
subtitle: "The container divs, and how they find their titles."
description: "Worked examples of the panel, card, card-grid, card-footer, and highlight divs, including the two ways a card gets a footer."
---

A container is a fenced div with a class.
The [Reference](../reference.qmd#divs) lists the classes and their attributes.
This page shows the source, and the behaviour the reference tables cannot carry.

## Panel

A panel is a bordered region with an optional header.

```markdown
::: {.panel title="A panel" style="accent"}

The body of the panel.

:::
```

`style` takes one of ten theme names: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `caution`, `neutral`, `subtle`, `emphasis`, `accent`, and `outline`.
It defaults to `subtle`.

An `icon` attribute puts one character before the title.

### The title comes from the first heading

A panel with no `title` attribute takes its title from the first heading inside it, and that heading is removed from the body.

```markdown
::: {.panel style="info"}

## Method

The heading above becomes the panel title.

:::
```

The same rule applies to a card and to an executive summary.

## Card

A card is a titled box.

```markdown
::: {.card title="Coverage" style="outlined"}

Ninety-nine per cent of lines are covered.

:::
```

`style` takes `subtle`, `outlined`, or `filled`, and defaults to `subtle`.

`colour` takes a hex code or a colour name, and it is honoured in both HTML and Typst output.
In HTML it becomes the `--card-accent` custom property.

## The two ways to give a card a footer

A card footer can be written as an explicit div:

```markdown
::: {.card title="Release"}

The body of the card.

::: {.card-footer}

Published on 1 March.

:::

:::
```

It can also be written as a horizontal rule.
Everything after the rule becomes the footer:

```markdown
::: {.card title="Release"}

The body of the card.

---

Published on 1 March.

:::
```

The two forms produce the same markup.
Use the rule when the footer is one line, and the div when the footer holds more than one block.

## Card grid

A card grid lays cards out in columns.

```markdown
::: {.card-grid columns="2"}

::: {.card title="First"}

The first card.

:::

::: {.card title="Second"}

The second card.

:::

:::
```

A card inside a grid is rendered by the grid itself, not on its own.

### The default number of columns depends on the format

`columns` defaults to `3` in HTML output and to `2` in a Reveal.js deck, because two cards fill a slide better than three.
The reference gives `3`, which is the value the schema declares and the value HTML uses.
Write `columns` when a deck and a page must match.

## Highlight

A highlight block emphasises a passage.

```markdown
::: {.highlight}

The sentence that matters most.

:::
```

It takes no attributes.
In Typst output it is wrapped in a template function.
In HTML it is styled by the stylesheet alone, so it carries no generated markup of its own.

## Executive summary

An executive summary is a titled block with decorative corner brackets.

```markdown
::: {.executive-summary}

Three sentences on what the report found.

:::
```

`title` defaults to `Executive Summary`.

`show-corner-brackets` removes the brackets, and only the literal `false` does so:

```markdown
::: {.executive-summary title="In brief" show-corner-brackets="false"}

Three sentences on what the report found.

:::
```

## Where the containers appear

The [rendered report](../preview.pdf) on this site carries a panel, and it is built by `mcanouil-typst` as the site publishes.
